meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: a large formal meal for many people

examples.text: У нас сегодня очень важный банкет.
examples.trans: We have a very important banquet today.
A lavish banquet was hosted in the restaurant.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.
Secondary conversational sense ('bigger') (comparative of большой) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to take', forming an aspectual pair with 'взять'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: 'взять на работу' = to give someone a job
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

включать.gloss: to turn on, to plug in

meanings.en: to switch on, to plug in
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to turn on', forming an aspectual pair with 'включить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Ninul, plug in the soldering iron.

examples.text: Он всегда включает свет на кухне.
examples.trans: He always switches on the kitchen light.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to tremble', forming an aspectual pair with 'задрожать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Его руки немного дрожат от усталости.
examples.trans: His hands are shaking a bit from exhaustion.
Your face is pale, your hands are shaking a bit.
Why are you trembling so much?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: красная икра = red (salmon) caviar, чёрная икра = black caviar

examples.text: Мама говорила, что у меня на икру аллергия.
examples.trans: Mum said I'm allergic to caviar.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'or', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to swear', forming an aspectual pair with 'поклясться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Клянусь честью повара, я не брал твой японский нож!
examples.trans: I swear on my honor as a cook, I did not take your Japanese knife!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

examples.text: Я никогда в жизни не пробовал такой вкусной утки!
examples.trans: I have never in my life tasted such delicious duck!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nothing') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('never mind, it's okay') (as a reply on its own) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I didn't understand a thing, Arkash.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'venison' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И ту оленину тоже унёс я!
examples.trans: And I also took that venison away!
I don't give a damn about your venison!

плевать.gloss: not to care, couldn't care less (+ dative)

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'not to care'.

examples.text: Если тебе плевать на дочь, то мне нет!
examples.trans: If you don't care about our daughter, I do!
My parents don't care about me.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('please') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('you're welcome') (answer to thanks) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('here you are') (handing something over) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.en: half a kilogram, half a kilo
meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'half a kilo', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Buy half a kilo of cheese.
And the half-kilo of expensive caviar?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'after' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'анный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('devoted, loyal').

examples.trans: I am devoted to the chef.
My friends are loyal to me.

examples.text: Мои люди преданы мне до конца.
examples.trans: My people are loyal to me to the end.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'device, apparatus' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do not turn on the device!
Chef, please do not turn on the device!

examples.text: Шеф, мы уже выключили все шумные приборы.
examples.trans: Chef, we have already turned off all noisy equipment.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to forgive', forming an aspectual pair with 'прощать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('excuse me, sorry') (imperative: прости / простите) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
about something: рассказать о + prepositional
ironic: Сталину расскажите = tell that to Stalin
Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'neighboring' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: В соседнем зале играет тихая музыка.
examples.trans: Quiet music plays in the neighboring hall.

examples.text: За соседним столиком сидели приятные люди.
examples.trans: Pleasant people were sitting at the next table.
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Russian determiner/pronoun ('that') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'красть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'красть'.

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'нести'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to carry away', forming an aspectual pair with 'уносить'.

examples.trans: Carry him away from the kitchen quickly.

examples.text: Унеси его с кухни прямо сейчас!
examples.trans: Carry him away from the kitchen right now!

examples.text: И ту оленину тоже унёс я!
examples.trans: And I also took that venison away!

ходить.gloss: to walk, to go (on foot, regularly)

meanings.en: to walk, to go on foot
meanings.note: back and forth or habitually; one trip in one direction: идти

examples.text: Мальчик ходит на костылях. А она ещё и активистка.
examples.trans: The boy walks on crutches. And she's an activist, too.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you want me to tell you honestly?

examples.text: Всё честно, Лёха. Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: It's all fair, Lyokha. Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
